Where it began

Joe Root was born on 30 December 1990 and grew up in Dore, on the edge of Sheffield. He went to King Ecgbert School, and at 15 won a cricket scholarship to Worksop College. His club was Sheffield Collegiate, where Michael Vaughan had once played; the former England captain became something of a mentor to him.

Cricket runs in the household. His younger brother Billy plays for Glamorgan.

The player

Root came into the England side in India in 2012, batting at six and making 73 on debut. A year later he scored his first Test hundred at Headingley, his home ground, the first Yorkshireman ever to do so there. He went on to captain England from 2017 to 2022, and was asked to lead them again in 2026.

By October 2026 he had played 169 Tests and made 14,278 runs at 50.45, with 41 hundreds and a highest score of 262, made at Multan in 2024 during a stand of 454 with Harry Brook. Only one man has scored more Test runs. He has also captained England in 68 Tests, winning 30, and has held 220 catches, more than any Test fielder but one.

What made him special

Root makes batting look like a conversation rather than an argument. He keeps the scoreboard moving, nudging singles and finding the boundary when it is needed, and he has scored runs all over the world, from Headingley to Multan. In December 2025 he added his first Test hundred in Australia, at the Gabba. He stands at first slip, bowls handy off-spin, and has 74 Test wickets to show for it.

For a while, around his first spell as captain, his fifties had a habit of stopping short of three figures, and he heard plenty about it. The hundreds have since arrived in such numbers that the complaint now seems rather quaint.

Away from the middle

He was a Wisden Cricketer of the Year in 2014 and the ICC Test Cricketer of the Year in 2021, and became an MBE in 2020, honoured for what he has given the game. He was part of the side that won the 2019 World Cup, where he was England's top scorer. Away from cricket, he follows Sheffield United.

And finally

In 2014 at Trent Bridge he and James Anderson put on 198 for the last wicket, a world record that says a good deal about Root's ability to bring out the best in a partner. And his best Test bowling, five wickets for eight runs, is the kind of analysis most part-time spinners only see in their dreams.
